Tabulate the distribution of the codes within each actor

Source: R/state_distribution_htna.R
state_distribution_htna.Rd

state_distribution_htna() returns the state distribution of a network: how often each code occurs and its share of the events of its group. For an htna network the group is the actor type, so the table shows how each actor divides its activity over its own codes; for a network without an actor partition all codes form one group, "all".

state_distribution_htna() runs Nestimate's state_distribution() and returns a data frame with one row per group and code. For an htna network it is the same table as frequencies_htna(); the function is provided under its general name for code written for other network types.

Usage

state_distribution_htna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna(), or another network.

...

Unused for htna networks.

Value

A data frame with one row per group and code and columns group, state, count and proportion (proportions sum to one within each group).

See also

frequencies_htna(), state_frequencies_htna() for the pooled table.

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
state_distribution_htna(net)
#>    group     state count proportion
#> 1     AI   Execute  3258 0.38100807
#> 2  Human   Request  3104 0.28751389
#> 3  Human   Specify  2920 0.27047054
#> 4     AI       Ask  2416 0.28254005
#> 5  Human Frustrate  1829 0.16941460
#> 6     AI      Plan  1620 0.18945153
#> 7  Human     Check  1298 0.12022971
#> 8  Human   Inquire   853 0.07901074
#> 9  Human    Refine   792 0.07336050
#> 10    AI    Report   705 0.08244650
#> 11    AI  Delegate   295 0.03449889
#> 12    AI    Repair   257 0.03005496
